record.paper_title: Invitation to H-systems in higher dimensions: known results, new facts, and related open problems
record.original_question: Let Omega be an open subset of R^n, let H: R^{n+1} -> R be bounded and Lipschitz, and let u=(u^1,...,u^{n+1}) be in W^{1,n}(Omega,R^{n+1}) as a weak solution of the H-system -div(|grad u|^{n-2} grad u) = H(u) J_u. If k of the coordinate functions u^i are bounded, for some k in {1,2,...,n}, must u be continuous?

evidence.quote: Problem 3.4. Let u = (u1 , u2 , . . . , un+1 ) ∈ W 1,n (Ω, Rn+1 ) be a weak solution of the H-system (2.5), where H : Rn+1 → R is bounded and Lipschitz.
Assume that k of the coordinate functions ui are bounded, where k ∈ {1, 2, . . . , n}. Is u continuous?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $n \geq 2$ and let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be an open set. Let $H : \mathbb{R}^{n+1} \to \mathbb{R}$ be a bounded Lipschitz function. Consider a weak solution $u = (u^1, u^2, \ldots, u^{n+1}) \in W^{1,n}(\Omega, \mathbb{R}^{n+1})$ of the H-system
$$-\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{n-2} \nabla u\bigr) \;=\; H(u)\, J_u,$$
where $J_u$ denotes the vector whose $i$-th component is the Jacobian determinant of the map $(u^1,\dots,\widehat{u^i},\dots,u^{n+1}) : \Omega \to \mathbb{R}^n$ (with the $i$-th coordinate omitted), with appropriate sign so that the right-hand side represents the prescribed mean curvature term. Suppose that for some integer $k \in \{1, 2, \ldots, n\}$, exactly $k$ of the coordinate functions $u^i$ are bounded in $\Omega$ (the remaining $n+1-k$ need not be bounded beyond their $W^{1,n}$ membership). 

Must $u$ be continuous in $\Omega$?
artifact.status_search_result: Known results establish continuity of $W^{1,n}$ weak solutions to the n-dimensional H-system when the full solution $u$ is bounded (in $L^\infty$), or under stronger integrability such as $u \in W^{n-1,n}$. The question of whether boundedness of only $k \in \{1,\ldots,n\}$ coordinate components (partial boundedness) is sufficient to imply continuity appears not to have been resolved in the literature; standard regularity techniques (Hardy/BMO, Rivière–Uhlenbeck decomposition, Coifman–Rochberg–Weiss commutator) use boundedness of the whole map. No source establishing or disproving the partial-boundedness implication was found.

status_evidence.title: Regularity of weak solutions of n-dimensional H-systems
status_evidence.snippet: Under the assumption u ∈ W^{n-1,n}(D, R^{n+1}) (or boundedness of u), Hölder continuity is proven via Hardy spaces, BMO, and the Rivière–Uhlenbeck decomposition.
status_evidence.claim: Continuity is known under full boundedness or higher-order Sobolev assumptions, but partial-component boundedness is not addressed.
